note: Concept mockups with synthetic records. Display order defines option numbering. No prototype or production interaction was implemented.

options.prompt:
Create realistic, production-quality UI design with clear hierarchy, strong typography and purposeful spacing. Use case ui-mockup. Reference image is the EXISTING Regovise app: retain the Regovise serif wordmark, warm white/lavender/purple brand (#8f2ee8 primary, #2b0b4d text), light readable sans serif product typography, slim border/divider vocabulary. Redesign hierarchy for professional security analysts and ISSOs managing Federal RMF system ATOs. It is a desktop web app 1440 x 1024, no browser chrome, no device bezel, no multiple screens or inset variants. Current date anchor October 11, 2026 America/New_York; all visible dates near this date must be correct and plausible. All records are synthetic design examples, add a small 'Example workspace' label. Do not imply existing Regovise functionality or actual ATO decisions were verified.
Global sidebar exactly seven simple items: My Work, Systems, Controls, Evidence & Tests, Risk & POA&M, Authorization, Monitoring. Footer Tools and Administration links. Top bar has a system context selector 'Atlas API' and authorization case selector 'Agency RMF · Moderate', compact search, user 'Jordan Lee · ISSO'. Status language must distinguish authorization on file, preparation, review, evidence freshness, and risk; never use a compliance percentage as authorization. Full suite exists offscreen. Focused primary screen, one clear main action and at most two supporting content areas. Normal lists/tables use light row dividers, not every row as a card; no nested cards, no gratuitous charts/metric grids. Body 14–16px equivalent; no cropped or illegible UI. Restrained purple selection/CTA, labels rather than color alone. Preserve brand, reduce excessive nav/card density.
Design direction name: Task-first Analyst Desk. Show 'My Work' selected. Main title 'Good morning, Jordan' and one short line 'Review the work that can delay Atlas API authorization.' Main surface is one prioritized work queue with tabs 'Assigned to me' and 'Needs review', three genuine-looking rows: 'Review access-control evidence' (AC-2, Collected Oct 10, Needs review), 'Resolve overdue remediation' (POA&M-014, Due Oct 9, Overdue), 'Approve boundary update' (CM-8, Changed Oct 10, Needs ISSO review). Rows include system, owner and due/freshness context with muted metadata. A selected evidence row has a compact right details panel: 'Account inventory', 'Source: cloud IAM', 'Collected Oct 10, 2026', 'Control AC-2', 'Human review required', a primary purple 'Review evidence' button. Supporting quiet authorization summary shows 'Agency decision on file' and 'Next review Oct 16' separate from '2 evidence checks need attention'. No fabricated donut readiness score. Lots of whitespace, focused work-first UX, small secondary 'View system' link. Task-first structure must be clearly distinct from a system dashboard or narrative editor.

Design direction name: System Readiness Cockpit. Show Systems selected in sidebar. This screen is a focused system detail overview for an ISSO, not a generic enterprise dashboard. Title 'Atlas API' with description 'System owner: Alex Kim · ISSO: Jordan Lee'. A quiet secondary header says 'Agency authorization on file' with a link 'View signed decision', separate from 'Current review: In preparation'. Local navigation Overview, Boundary, Assets, Dependencies, Team with Overview active. One spacious central 'What needs attention' surface lists three plain rows: 'Evidence changed for 2 controls' (Review updated evidence, Oct 10), 'POA&M-014 is overdue' (Owner Alex Kim, Oct 9), 'Boundary update needs approval' (Shared services component added, Oct 10). One main purple CTA 'Open review work'. Adjacent narrow 'Authorization case' detail column: 'Agency RMF · Moderate', 'Stage: Preparing review package', 'Decision record: On file', 'Next scheduled review: Oct 16, 2026', 'Package changes since last decision: 3', small 'Open case' link. Below main surface a single modest 'Operating history' list with 'Oct 10 · Account evidence refreshed' and 'Oct 9 · Shared component proposed'. Avoid metric-card wall, percentage charts, deceptive green authorization based on task completion. More breathing room and system context than task-first screen; user should immediately understand which system and authorization case this work concerns.

Design direction name: Evidence-linked Control Workbench. Show Controls selected. This is a focused working screen for an ISSO and control owner. Breadcrumb 'Atlas API / Controls / AC-2'. Title 'AC-2 · Account Management'. Header secondary metadata 'Owner: Jordan Lee' and label 'Draft revision · Needs review'. Main split working area: a slim left control-family list with AC-1 approved, AC-2 selected needs review, AC-3 needs evidence, AU-2 approved; center has local tabs Implementation, Evidence, Assessment, History with Implementation selected and a readable draft narrative in an editor: 'Privileged accounts are assigned to approved roles. Account inventory is reviewed by the system owner, and inactive accounts are disabled through the identity provider.' Immediately below one unobtrusive 'Supporting evidence' group with source-linked rows 'Account inventory · cloud IAM · Oct 10, 2026 · Review required' and 'Access review record · Jordan Lee · Oct 8, 2026 · Approved'. Right sidebar a concise 'Review checklist': Implementation answers the requirement; Source evidence matches system boundary; Two evidence revisions need confirmation. An explicit small statement 'Draft content must be reviewed before use in the authorization package.' One main purple CTA 'Request review'; supporting 'Save draft' low emphasis. No machine-generated verdict 'compliant', no compliance percentage, no fake auto-ATO button. Use careful typesetting, professional readable narrative-editor ergonomics, whitespace, light row dividers. Make the control/evidence/reviewer linkage visually clear; distinct from both the task list and system overview.
